note: Placeholder values identical for both factions, except owner decisions 2026-11-11: wedge default, 10 m spacing, balanced cover preference (accept ~30 % longer routes to stay in cover). M4.4: boundM (length of one bound in fire and movement) and finalAssaultM (the last stretch rushed together) are game values, the same for both sides until a public source gives a difference (owner to review). D4a (owner answer 2026-11-14, rushes of 3-5 s and 15-20 m): boundM 30 -> 16 m, about 4.6 s at the 3.5 m/s run. M6.5c fire support: Battalion 120 mm mortars (Moerser 120 mm): game values for the time to first round, spread and cadence. Pulled forward from M8 by the owner (M6 review); low confidence. Step fire-support (owner 2026-11-13, Firefight S11): two ranging rounds land first (first one off by the aiming error, each seen fall cuts the error to 30 %), 20 s apart, then the 4-tube battery fires for effect in volleys (rounds 0.6 s apart, volleys every intervalSeconds); delaySeconds is now the time to the first ranging round (was 90/75 s to the first round); a mission within 100 m of a point already ranged on skips ranging. All game values, no public source (search extracts only): low. M8.1 smoke v2: a smoke round's cloud rises to smokeTopM 15 m and its burning filling feeds the plume at its place for smokeBurnSeconds (red phosphorus / HC fillings burn for a minute or more; game values, low, owner to review). M8.2a call-for-fire chain (game values, low, owner to review): of delaySeconds the radio call takes requestSeconds 15 and the flight flightSeconds (16 s: a section about 2 km back), the rest is computing and laying; splash is called 5 s before a round lands; rangingErrorM is now the battery's own first-round error (15 m per axis, meteorology and survey) and the target's location adds 5 m + 7 % of the caller's range for a map or eye estimate (eye range estimates err 10-20 %), 2 m + 0.5 % with a laser rangefinder (so at 500 m an estimate misses about 3x as far); a registered or planned point keeps what was left after its adjustment. M8.2b observers (game values, low, owner to review): the caller or any man of his platoon who sees a ranging round fall (a crewman through his sight, with its laser if it has one) reads it; the best reader corrects: the error left is rangingCorrection x a skill factor (1.5 at skill 0 to 0.6 at skill 1) of the old one, plus his reading error (3 m + 1 % of his distance to the fall by eye, 2 m with a laser, x the same skill factor) M8.4 (game values unless noted, owner to review): an off-map artillery battery as `artillery` — PzH 2000 (155 mm, up to 10 rounds a minute, about 30 km with DM121: KNDS / Wikipedia extracts), 4 guns; first round after 150-180 s (request 20 s, flight 40 s), ranging 45 s apart, battery error 25-35 m, dispersion 45-55 m, airburst 8 m over the target (multi-option fuzes), danger close 600 m (a call this close to own men needs the danger-close flag), the battery displaces for 600 s after every 3 missions (abstract counter-battery); illumination rounds for mortars and artillery. M10.3a casualtyCarePriority (how readily a man leaves the fight for a wounded comrade, a factor in core/medical.json carers willingness): 0.5, the same for every side, game value (no public source for a national difference), low. M9.5: a point located through a drone's camera (4 m + 2 % of the drone's slant range) and by an off-map fixed-wing reconnaissance drone (10 m), and falls read through them (3 m, 6 m): game values, low (search extracts describe drone-adjusted fire as far faster, no public error figures).

dismount.note: Owner Q22 (M7.2): sourced per side. Bundeswehr principle 'mounted as long as possible, dismounted as briefly as possible', dismount where the enemy cannot observe; no published distance, so 300 m is a game choice inside the 500 m grenadier-tank spacing (docs/research/dismount.md). M7.3: afterwards the Pumas stay where they dropped the squads and support them by fire from there (overwatch; Bundeswehr articles: the IFVs engage from a covered position; docs/research/dismount.md, low).

identityTag.note: Every soldier wears the Erkennungsmarke (two halves, counted as two items); from a man confirmed dead a comrade breaks off one half and takes it; the other stays with the body (bundeswehr.de 'Erkennungsmarke', search extract: medium).
